ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, D is a point on $BC$, $AD=BD$, $\angle B=40^\circ$, and $\triangle ADE$ is symmetrical to $\triangle ADB$ with respect to $AD$. What is the measure of $\angle CDE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AD=BD$ and $\angle B=40^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle B=40^\circ=\angle BAD$, \\
therefore, $\angle ADB=180^\circ-\left(\angle BAD+\angle B\right)=100^\circ$ and $\angle ADC=\angle B+\angle BAD=80^\circ$, \\
since $\triangle ADE$ is symmetric to $\triangle ADB$ with respect to $AD$, \\
it follows that $\angle ADE=\angle ADB=100^\circ$, \\
thus, $\angle CDE=\angle ADE-\angle ADC=100^\circ-80^\circ=\boxed{20^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, B, D, C are on the same horizontal straight line, and D is between B and C; A is above line BC, and AB, AD, AC are connected; E is located at the lower right of D, and DE and AE are connected; the ray DC starting from D is inside ∠ADE. Reasoning: Because D is on BC, ∠B, namely ∠ABD = 40°. Also because AD = BD, △ABD is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles ∠BAD = ∠ABD = 40°. Therefore ∠ADB = 180° - 40° - 40° = 100°. Since DB and DC are opposite rays on the same straight line, ∠ADC = 180° - ∠ADB = 80°. △ADE and △ADB are symmetric about AD, so ∠ADE = ∠ADB = 100°. In the figure, DC is inside ∠ADE, therefore ∠CDE = ∠ADE - ∠ADC = 100° - 80° = 20°.
